answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a licensed truffle-hound season on a named knoll, where the handler and one trained dog wander the violet-shaded woods at dawn and every find is weighed and logged by an independent mycologist. Random spot-checks summon the holder and that exact dog to the knoll within a day, and one handler cannot run two dogs on the same morning, so no parallel farming. Each extra fake identity costs another trained dog, another season of dawn walks, another human handler, and a license fee in outside money that doubles per identity on the same funding trail.
